text: Para-methoxybenzaldehyde at 10/1 and 150 uL sample volume; packet prediction 10.823808670043945/36.8455696105957 mL. Measured 100 uL row 319e89d7000731f64e7f gave 4.78/36.82 mL. This loading contrast tests whether its unusually early onset is associated with loading, as seen for m127, or remains an isolated observation.
Adds a methylated aromatic ketone at 10/1, supporting local substitution-response learning without propagating the m116 failure to all ethers.

Targets a methyl quinoline at 2/1 DCM with a high predicted V1 and broad interval, testing positional and heteroaromatic effects relative to the measured m90 and m141 late regimes `6a4e95d2a3cca31094a1` and `51f4126a3aadb3239225`.

m38 at 10/1, 50 uL begins a matched 10/1–20/1 pair for a fluorene-containing aryl ketone with only the 2/1 region measured in a2f5638c0f2528673e4e. It tests transfer of steep fused-aryl-ketone responses into a structurally different ring environment; the existing anchor uses 100 uL. Frozen V1/V2: 9.627182960510254/35.13527297973633 mL.
Low-composition trifluoromethoxy dihalogenated aromatic provides a compact halogenated-ether anchor against the higher-composition m153 condition.
Neutral hydrocarbon-like aromatic control at weak eluent, constraining the lower-retention region and complementing measured m14 and m133 controls 6325c295ee77a229bbdc and 469630617554d93aef66.

m13 at 10/1 and 150 ul tests whether the extreme ratio response is primarily a loading effect or a ratio-dependent endpoint transition, using the measured 1/1 and 5/1 references 81507d463506a9e65e73 and 5d530b2f228ed39ff952.

m72 at 10/1 with PE and 150 ul extends the response into the PE-rich regime while changing loading volume. It tests whether V1 and V2 develop the decoupled tail behavior seen in measured m90 row 96710afeabc594baa359.
A low-ratio chalcone-like scaffold at 1/1 supplies a neutral aromatic carbonyl anchor, useful for distinguishing ordinary carbonyl behavior from the nonlinear tails measured for m118 and m114.

Measure m177 at 0/1 with the same 140.6 mg loading and DCM volume used in the measured 10/1 row ce14dd2481560a984aea. This directly extends the nitrobenzophenone endpoint curve after the large V2 failures in ce14dd2481560a984aea and aa43fe84c0d8c825fe58.

The 50/1 m177 condition is a deliberately strong extrapolation from the observed m177 points ce14dd2481560a984aea, aa43fe84c0d8c825fe58, and 34aaca6f7a0768d743fe; its large predicted V2 range can reveal whether the late-endpoint behavior continues at weaker eluent.

This 5/1 m204 low-loading point probes the solvent region between the low-retention 1/1 observations a3560ac8164465dbb406 and c46b86dae7e6845f08cd and the very late 10/1 alcohol observation 73502a52708e4f9c2391.

Complete the m81 5/1 loading series at 55.5 mg. Measured fefecd79dc057980f62c and a9500e468002e41eceeb finish at 18.57 and 9.23 mL at 111 and 166.5 mg, respectively; this label distinguishes a loading trend from an isolated short-finish observation.

Obtain a near-replicate of m73's exceptional 1/1 observation, predicted 14.11/19.91 mL. Recorded conditions match except for a density difference yielding 0.01 mg extra sample. Together with the lower-load and 2/1 selections, it distinguishes reproducibility, amount dependence and ratio locality.
A phenolic aldehyde probes whether donor capability adds finish delay beyond ordinary aromatic aldehyde behavior, extending the measured m117 and m197 contrasts.
A weak-solvent terpene aldehyde tests whether delayed finishes occur in a less heteroatom-rich aldehyde topology, complementing measured m49 behavior 766525688b9ba3f69efe.
A methoxy aryl ketone bridges simple ketones and oxygenated aromatic carbonyls for local transition learning, complementing measured m115 behavior 122fbec0df9ecf1c5d89.
A bromoacetophenone at strong eluent supplies a simple aryl-ketone endpoint anchor before weak-solvent broadening and complements measured m34 and m43 controls.

A high-loading dicarbonyl-like scaffold targets delayed V2 learning in a topology distinct from simpler ketones and complements measured m166 and m178 failures 80de1b57c56257d2ecae and 0c5c35afb3a24375c153.

A bromonaphthaldehyde tests whether aldehyde finish tails transfer from smaller aromatics to fused-ring systems, extending measured m49 and m194 evidence 766525688b9ba3f69efe and d7895c522a1a46a1175c.
A high-loading phenolic aldehyde tests donor-plus-aldehyde coupling against measured m186 loading/ratio points a352b1f204da6fcfd385 and c45057c2cab40f4fa2be.
This aryl diketone at 50/1 DCM is an endpoint-width probe for polycarbonyl behavior, using the measured m166 and m94 tails 4c2ad10692512e8f23b8 and ffc70e28db22d1cc1f3f as family evidence.
A high-loading stilbene under 0/1 DCM supplies a nonpolar loading control, useful for separating injection effects from the scaffold-specific shifts seen in m72 and m211.
This high-uncertainty diaryl diketone at 50/1 DCM directly probes the V2-tail region highlighted by measured m94, m95, and m166 outcomes, including 1a55639d058c08a1a06e and 80de1b57c56257d2ecae.
This substituted aryl ketone at 10/1 PE extends carbonyl condition coverage and can test whether the strong ketone response observed for m40 generalizes across substitution patterns.
This aryl aldehyde at 1/1 PE extends aldehyde substitution coverage and tests whether delayed V2 finishes persist outside the measured m192 and m117 examples.
This anisyl ketone at 1/1 PE adds a neutral aromatic carbonyl point near the measured condition-response family for m40 and m114.
A fused ether aldehyde at 1/1 tests whether aldehyde behavior transfers from the severe m28 result 351c17dfa8f46a8cb40 to a less strongly loaded heterocyclic scaffold.
This trifluoro polycarbonyl at 10/1 targets endpoint behavior near measured m166 tail examples 20acd2ae49790ab82053 and d9ebd22828036fc4c7e6.
An unsaturated aldehyde at 1/1 PE tests whether aldehyde delay is already present in a compact, less acceptor-rich topology compared with m28 and m197 measured failures.
A simple aryl ketone at 50/1 samples the high-solvent neutral carbonyl slope and provides a control against transferring the m25 and m26 tail corrections universally.
A substituted aryl ketone at 5/1 probes a moderate carbonyl slope between ordinary controls and the severe measured m25 and m95 V2 tails.
A brominated aldehyde at 0/1 gives a weak-solvent aldehyde boundary point, complementing the measured narrow aldehyde result b73454f4c6942f4deb70 and severe m28 result 351c17dfa8f46a8cb40.
An anisaldehyde-like scaffold at 1/1 tests whether aldehyde V2 broadening is general or depends on the substitution pattern responsible for measured m28 and m197 tails.
Quinoline at 1/1 PE supplies a fused ring-nitrogen control distinct from the severe pyridyl ketone observation 49201b5817f204116f7f and the ordinary m211 controls.

m178 at 5/1 fills the solvent gap between measured 2/1 5d450444eb031c873584 and 10/1 634f21e11a8442494ce3. It directly tests the hypothesis that completion responds independently of onset in a multifunctional ketone.

m118 at 20/1, 100 ul directly extends 10/1 observation 319e89d7000731f64e04, measured at 4.78/36.82 mL. The predicted 22.05/52.15 mL response tests whether onset catches up with completion in methoxybenzaldehyde, informed by the distinct thioether-aldehyde curve in d54c93a11164b4abac6e.

m177 at 10/1, 150 ul completes a fixed-loading 10/20/50 curve with 5e276c1730fc0a9deba7 and b514312eda7950cdcf1c. The forecast is 4.77/25.39 mL. Measuring it locates the emergence of long completion while testing whether onset remains early, independently of the selected 50-ul curve.
A flexible carbonyl heteroaromatic tests whether broad V2 behavior extends beyond fused aromatic systems such as measured m194 in d7895c522a1a46a1175c.
This high-ratio m39 experiment samples a carbonyl scaffold with a broad predicted response and can extend the measured high-ratio carbonyl behavior represented by f31a89256d8ee4192d55.
